paper_summary: Phenolic (phenol-formaldehyde) syntactic foam filled with dry fly ash cenospheres (50:50 proportion, 0.70 reinforcement volume fraction by resin burnout) was used as the core of glass/epoxy faced sandwich panels, either plain (SF) or confined in honeycomb grid cells of 20, 15, 10 and 5 mm (SFK20-SFK5). Tensile, compressive, flexural (long and short beam) and three-rail shear properties were measured in flatwise (out-of-plane) and edgewise (in-plane) configurations per ASTM standards. Confining the foam in the honeycomb grid raised the mechanical properties by 20-180%, with the smallest (5 mm) cell size best; the phenolic foam was thermally stable to 450 C.

extraction_notes: All moduli were reported in GPa and converted to MPa (x1000). Properties are those of the sandwich panel (syntactic foam core + glass/epoxy face skins), not of the bare foam; the honeycomb grid and face skins are recorded in additional_fillers. particle_volume_fraction=0.70 is the reinforcement volume fraction of the syntactic foam from the resin burnout test (Table 1); the text also states a 50:50 foam mixing proportion, which is not explicitly labelled as weight or volume, so particle_weight_fraction was left null. Test temperature was not stated (ambient assumed but left null). Strain rate was not reported; only a constant crosshead displacement rate of 0.5 mm/min is given, and no gauge length is provided to convert it, so strain_rate_per_s is null. Strain at failure, density and energy absorption are only visible in stress-strain figures (Figs. 2-6) and are not tabulated, so they are left null. Long-beam and short-beam flexure are distinguished in test.specimen_notes. process_route recorded as vacuum_assisted because the resin-impregnated glass fabrics were vacuum bonded to the packed foam core.
